title: The Orion Bar region (NIRCam image)
caption: The Orion Bar region of the Orion Nebula, imaged by the James Webb Space Telescope
celestial: [BOM2000] d203-506, HH 520, Messier 42, Orion Bar, Orion Nebula · constellation Orion · about 1400 light-years away (source figure)
credit: ESA/Webb, NASA, CSA, M. Zamani (ESA/Webb), the PDRs4All ERS Team

recognition.text: Official ESA/Webb press-release image. No published audience rating.

story: Layers of colorful, cloudy material fill this scene. The upper left is brightly lit and full of thin wisps in pale pink and blue, while a thick, denser bar of orange material cuts diagonally across the lower right, fading darker toward the corner, where two very bright stars sit with long spikes. This is the Orion Bar, part of the Orion Nebula, seen by Webb's NIRCam.

The region is bathed in harsh ultraviolet light from the Trapezium Cluster. That radiation erodes gas and dust through photoevaporation, carving the cavities and filaments, and it makes molecules glow so astronomers can study them.

In this region, Webb data revealed the methyl cation, CH3+, for the first time, in the disc around a young star called d203-506. Its key role in interstellar carbon chemistry had been predicted since the 1970s, and it turned up where life-friendly planets might one day form.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.08 x 2.31 arcminutes) and distance (1400 light years), the frame spans roughly 0.8 × 0.9 light-years. Its light set out about 1,400 years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This near-infrared image from Webb's NIRCam uses many filters, running from purple and blue for the shortest wavelengths through cyan, green, yellow and orange to red for the longest, including filters for molecular hydrogen, water ice and PAH molecules.
understand.eye: This light is infrared and invisible to the eye, so the colors map wavelengths and chemistry we cannot see.

explore: The two bright stars belong to the θ² Orionis system. The brightest, θ² Orionis A, is surrounded by bright red puffs of dust reflecting its light, and it is visible to the naked eye because it is itself three tightly bound stars.
In the top left, a tiny star sits inside a long dusty cocoon made from its own eroding disc, with a round shockwave moving through the gas around it.
alt: Colorful layers of cloudy material, with pale pink and blue wisps at upper left, a thick orange bar crossing the lower right, and two very bright stars with long spikes.
